assertions.name: operator_markov_route_is_not_canonical_ladder_target
assertions.source: PR #1875 follow-up: tests whether R := tr_M(trefoil) / [Q_A · cos(α_eff)] IS the canonical Prod_k(1+c_k u^k) ladder. Gate: c_2 must = -1 (PR #1786 canonical). If c_2 ASSERTS -1, the operator-Markov is canonical (positive result); if c_2 != -1, the operator-Markov is NOT the canonical ladder target (negative result narrowing the open question to per-rung operator identities). FAIL = the latter — passes this assertion by establishing the negative diagnostic. Combined with R's small local radius of convergence (~0.011) inconsistent with O(1) c_k ladder singularities (~1), the negative result is robust.

description: Extracts c_2..c_8 via local Taylor of R(u) around substrate u_0 ~ 0.00852 (where du/dt = 0.1398, NOT a branch point). Nonlinearly matches R(u_0+dv) against Q_base * Prod_k(1+c_k u^k). Gate: c_2 ~ -1 (PR #1786 canonical). Follow-up to PR #1875, which correctly proved u=0 ladder impossible but overstated the scope (u_0 ladder IS well-defined). All series arithmetic in mpmath (dps=50) for speed; sympy only for small piece-wise Taylor expansions.

data.interpretation: GATE FAIL is a meaningful negative result. R := tr_M(trefoil) / [Q_A cos(α_eff)] is NOT the canonical ladder target. The c_k are PER-RUNG operator identities (PR #1786 c_2=-1 lives at N=2 OPERATOR level, not as a Taylor coefficient of tr_M). Aggregating per-rung identities via tr_M of the trefoil gives the wrong global function for the Prod(1+c_k u^k) ansatz. Narrows the open question to: what is the per-rung operator identity for c_k at N=k?
